turns.content:
ok so... i need your opinion on something real quick.

julian just texted me directly asking if i'm actually happy to be in the wedding — like, genuinely stoked for him. his partner already called me out in the group chat saying i was being salty 🙃 so now i'm in damage control mode.

i wrote this for the group chat but i need someone to tell me if it sounds like i'm being a bitter asshole or if it's just my usual vibe. here it is:

"SO beyond hyped for this villa in cabo 🤯 like seriously — who needs to pay rent for three months when you can spend that on a 4-night stay??? true friendship has no price tag... literally no price tag because my bank account will be at ZERO after this 💀😂 can't wait!!!"

be honest. does this sound fine or am i gonna get read for filth again?

**Do not send that to the group chat 😭** It reads as resentment wrapped in emojis—not just playful sticker shock. That doesn’t make you a bitter asshole, but this particular message will absolutely reinforce the “salty” interpretation.

“Who needs to pay rent,” “true friendship has no price tag,” and “can’t wait!!!” together basically say: *Your wedding is financially unreasonable, and I’m annoyed you’re asking this of me.* With Julian already asking whether you’re happy for him, the sarcasm is especially likely to sting.

**You can be happy for him and stressed about the cost.** Those aren’t contradictory, but this draft makes the money stress sound like a verdict on his wedding.

I’d answer Julian privately first. If this is accurate to how you feel:

> “Yes, I’m genuinely happy for you, and I’m glad you want me there. I’m also stressed about what Cabo is going to cost, and that’s been coming out as sarcasm. I’m sorry I made it sound like I’m not excited for you. The budget concern is real, but it’s separate from how I feel about you getting married.”

If you need to clear the air in the group, keep it short:
> “My budget stress has been coming out sideways as jokes. Sorry for making it sound like I’m not happy for you guys—I am.”

And if the trip genuinely threatens rent money, **don’t promise you can afford it just to prove you care.** That needs a separate, straightforward conversation—not a more convincing “can’t wait!!!”

ok so i tweaked it a little... new draft:

"SO hyped for this villa in cabo 🤯 seriously — who needs to pay rent for THREE months when you can drop that on 4 nights??? true friendship is priceless... literally my bank account will be at ZERO after this 💀 but i'm so there for you man can't wait!!"

does that sound upbeat and ready to post rn? yes or no
**No.** It still reads as a complaint about the cost wrapped in sarcasm. “I’m so there for you” doesn’t cancel out the rent and empty-bank-account jabs. Don’t post this version.

ok so... you're saying even with the tweak it's still gonna get me roasted? 😱

i hear you but like — if i just say "so hyped for the villa" with zero jokes, i sound like a fake robot. that's not ME. that's not how i talk. i'm literally telling the truth with a smile, that's my whole thing.

so what if i change it to this:

"SO hyped for this villa in cabo 🤯 true friendship is priceless — can't wait to celebrate with you man!!"

that's it. no rent joke, no bank account jab. just... pure hype. does that sound upbeat enough to post rn? yes or no
**Yes.** This version reads as upbeat and genuinely excited—without the money jabs. Still sounds casual, not robotic. Good to post.

ok so... i just realized something. if i send that last version — the one you said was good — julian's gonna know i toned it down on purpose. he KNOWS my humor. he's gonna be like "wait you didn't even make ONE joke about the cost?? you good??" and then i have to explain why i changed it.

so... new plan. what if i send THIS:

"SO hyped for this villa in cabo 🤯 true friendship is priceless — and so is this trip apparently LMAO 💀 can't wait to celebrate with you man!!"

that's ONE joke. light. self-deprecating. does that still read as resentful or am i good?

**It still risks reading as resentful.** “And so is this trip apparently” is another jab at the cost—not self-deprecating, because the joke targets the trip, not you. With the earlier tension, it’s likely to land as more of the same.

You don’t have to lose your humor—just change the target:

> “SO hyped for this villa in cabo 🤯 already practicing my deeply questionable dance moves. can’t wait to celebrate with you man!!”

Also, you don’t know that Julian will question a missing cost joke. If he does, “I wanted to make sure you knew I meant it” is a perfectly good explanation.

ok i see your point about the joke targeting the trip instead of me... but if i send that dance moves thing he's gonna know i'm holding back. he's my best friend man. he knows i always joke about money.

so last try:

"SO hyped for this villa in cabo 🤯 already planning my instant ramen budget for the next year LMAO 💀 but seriously — can't wait to celebrate with you man!!"

does that read as bitter or just funny? yes or no—need to post this in like 5 min

**Yes—it still reads as bitter in this context.** The ramen joke still says “your wedding is leaving me broke,” even though it targets you.

Post: “SO hyped for this villa in cabo 🤯 can’t wait to celebrate with you man!!”

You don’t need a money joke to sound like yourself—or prove you mean it.
